author: Lauren Martinez
title: Bon Secours expands child bereavement program to Portsmouth - NewsBreak
text:
By Lauren Martinez ,
4 hours ago
PORTSMOUTH, Va. (WAVY) —KIDZ N’ GRIEF is celebrating 25 years and is now offering the Bon Secours-created program to the Portsmouth community, bringing continuous support for children, teens and their families as they process feelings of sadness after loss.
Experiencing grief is inevitable, but no one should have to brave it alone. Bon Secours is putting special attention on helping kids in Portsmouth heal through KIDZ N’ GRIEF, after identifying a great need.
“One in 12 children in Virginia will be grieved by the death of a parent or sibling by the age of 18, and that number more than doubles by the age of 25,” said Ariane Walter, Bon Secours Hampton Roads bereavement and volunteer coordinator. “And that’s also not including grandparents, aunts, uncles, friends, cousins.”
Understanding and accepting someone close to you has died can be a lifelong journey, often requiring support beyond familial. The free program is volunteer-led.
“The volunteers, they’re trained, and we also have facilitators that help lead the groups,” said Simone Williams, Bon Secours Hampton Roads community outreach program manager. “The children interact with art projects, games and just role play activities. They’re also able to watch if they don’t want to participate and share. It’s completely up to them, but it’s a peer support group surrounded by caring adults that are there for support.”
Said Walter: “They’re dealing with sadness, perhaps depression, just lingering feelings and a battle with their emotions. I think making sure that they feel safe is the first step and making sure that they feel seen and heard.”
KIDZ N’ GRIEF is available to children ages five to 18. Currently Bon Secours serves roughly 130 kids between Newport News and Portsmouth and has developed a partnership with Portsmouth Public Schools with hopes to expand further.
“The children meet at an after-school setting at select Portsmouth schools twice a month,” Williams said. “One of the activities that we recently did was we took a trip to the Adventure Park at Virginia Beach, and the kids, they learned to believe in themselves despite the challenges they may face in life.”
KIDZ N’ GRIEF runs annually from September through June. Bon Secours’ weeklong grief camp, Mikey’s Camp, is also held in November. Applications are accepted for the camp until Sept. 15.
